subject: math
title: Patterns: Pattern Rules, Tables of Values and Decimal Patterns
seo_title: Grade 5 Patterns Math Worksheets: Pattern Rules, Tables of Values and Graphs (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Determine pattern rules and use them to extend patterns, make and justify predictions, and identify missing elements in repeating, growing, and shrinking patterns
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on patterns for the Ontario curriculum: growing, shrinking and repeating patterns, tables of values, pattern rules, decimal patterns with 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75, and graphs for making predictions. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: From term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps. In 4, 7, 10, 13 …, term 10 is 4 + 9 × 3 = 31.
key_sub: The term number is the place; the term value is the number in that place. Check every step of a pattern, not only the first one. In decimal patterns, 100 hundredths make 1 whole: 0.75 + 0.25 = 1.
body_html:
Growing and shrinking patterns

A growing pattern gets bigger and a shrinking pattern gets smaller. Find the change from each term to the next. Check every step, not only the first one.

Example 1

95, 88, 81, 74, ?

Each step subtracts 7. 74 − 7 = 67.

Answer: 67

Tables of values

Each number in a pattern is a term. Its place is the term number (1, 2, 3 …), and the number itself is the term value. A table of values shows both.

Pattern rules

A pattern rule can say how to get the next term (start at 4 and add 3 each time) or how to get a term from its term number (term number × 3 + 1). Both rules give 4, 7, 10, 13 …

Example 2

Which term number has a term value of 40 in 4, 7, 10, 13, …?

40 − 4 = 36, and 36 ÷ 3 = 12 jumps after term 1. So it is term 13. Check: 13 × 3 + 1 = 40.

Answer: term number 13

Decimal patterns

Count by 0.25, 0.5 or 0.75 like counting by quarters, halves or three-quarters. When the hundredths make 100, they make 1 whole.

Example 3

0.25, 0.5, 0.75, ?

0.75 + 0.25: 75 hundredths + 25 hundredths = 100 hundredths = 1.

Answer: 1

Graphs of patterns

Plot each term as a point (term number, term value). In a pattern that adds the same amount, the points lie in a straight line, so you can predict the next point.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using only the first step: 3, 6, 12, 24 is “add 3”Check every step. 3, 6, 12, 24 doubles, so the next term is 48
Mixing up the term number and the term valueThe term number is the place; the term value is the number in that place
Term 10 = term 1 + 10 jumpsFrom term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps
0.9 + 0.3 = 0.129 tenths + 3 tenths = 12 tenths = 1.2
Swapping a point: (16, 5)Write the term number first: (5, 16)

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about patterns in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 5 (Algebra, C1), students extend growing, shrinking and repeating patterns, find pattern rules, show patterns in tables of values and graphs, and make predictions. They also make patterns with decimal tenths and hundredths, such as 0.25, 0.5, 0.75.

faq.q: What is the difference between a term number and a term value?
faq.a: The term number is the place in the pattern (1st, 2nd, 3rd …) and the term value is the number in that place. In 5, 8, 11, 14, term number 3 has a term value of 11.

faq.q: How do you find the 10th term of a pattern like 4, 7, 10, 13?
faq.a: The pattern adds 3 each time, and from term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps. 4 + 9 × 3 = 31, so the 10th term is 31.

faq.q: How can I help my child with decimal patterns at home?
faq.a: Count by quarters with money: 25¢, 50¢, 75¢, $1.00 is the same as 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1. Then try counting by 0.5 or 0.75 and talk about what happens when the hundredths reach 100.

items.q:
What is the next term?
6, 10, 14, 18, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 4 each time (6 + 4 = 10). Next: 18 + 4 = 22.

items.q:
What is the next term?
120, 145, 170, 195, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 25 each time (120 + 25 = 145). Next: 195 + 25 = 220.
The pattern grows by 2500 each time (12 500 + 2500 = 15 000). Next: 20 000 + 2500 = 22 500.

items.q:
What is the next term?
15, 23, 31, 39, ?
items.e: The pattern grows by 8 each time (15 + 8 = 23). Next: 39 + 8 = 47.

items.q:
What is the next term?
90, 84, 78, 72, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 6 each time (90 − 6 = 84). Next: 72 − 6 = 66.

items.q:
What is the next term?
150, 138, 126, 114, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 12 each time (150 − 12 = 138). Next: 114 − 12 = 102.

items.q:
What is the next term?
1000, 875, 750, 625, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 125 each time (1000 − 125 = 875). Next: 625 − 125 = 500.

items.q:
What is the next term?
75, 70, 65, 60, ?
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 5 each time (75 − 5 = 70). Next: 60 − 5 = 55.

items.q:
What is the next term?
640, 320, 160, 80, ?
items.e: Each term is half of the one before (divide by 2): 80 ÷ 2 = 40. (Subtracting 320 like the first step does not work after that.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
1, 2, 4, 7, 11, ?
items.e: The jumps are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next jump is 5: 11 + 5 = 16. (Adding the first jump gives 12.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
2, 6, 18, 54, ?
items.e: Each term is 3 times the one before: 54 × 3 = 162. (Adding the first jump, 54 + 4 = 58, only works for the first step.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
3, 6, 12, 24, ?
items.e: The jumps are 3, 6, 12, so the pattern does not add the same amount. Each term is 2 times the one before: 24 × 2 = 48. (Adding the first jump, 24 + 3 = 27, only works for the first step.)

items.q:
What is the missing term?
35, 50, ?, 80, 95
items.e: The pattern grows by 15 each time. The missing term is 50 + 15 = 65. Check: 65 + 15 = 80.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
4500, 5000, 5500, ?, 6500
items.e: The pattern grows by 500 each time. The missing term is 5500 + 500 = 6000. Check: 6000 + 500 = 6500.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
100, 92, ?, 76, 68
items.e: The pattern shrinks by 8 each time. The missing term is 92 − 8 = 84. Check: 84 − 8 = 76.

items.q:
What is the missing term?
8, ?, 20, 26, 32
items.e: The pattern grows by 6 each time. The missing term is 8 + 6 = 14. Check: 14 + 6 = 20. (The jump from 8 to 20 is 12, but the missing term sits halfway between them.)

items.q: The pattern continues. How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure adds 2 tiles. Figure 4: 8 + 2 = 10.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many craft sticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 11, 16. Each figure adds 5 craft sticks. Figure 4: 16 + 5 = 21.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many craft sticks will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. Each figure adds 3 craft sticks. Figure 4: 10 + 3 = 13.

items.q: The pattern continues. How many tiles will Figure 4 need?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure adds 2 tiles. Figure 4: 7 + 2 = 9.

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The term value goes up by 3 each time. 11 + 3 = 14.

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The term value goes down by 5 each time. 50 − 5 = 45.

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The term value goes up by 4 each time. 18 + 4 = 22.

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The term value goes up by 7 each time. 30 + 7 = 37.

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The term value goes up by 5 each time. 17 + 5 = 22.

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 10?
items.e: From term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps of 4: 6 + 9 × 4 = 6 + 36 = 42. (22 is the value for term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 12?
items.e: From term 1 to term 12 there are 11 jumps of 5: 2 + 11 × 5 = 2 + 55 = 57. (22 is the value for term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 8?
items.e: From term 1 to term 8 there are 7 jumps of 8: 90 − 7 × 8 = 90 − 56 = 34. (58 is the value for term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 8?
items.e: From term 1 to term 8 there are 7 jumps of 3: 5 + 7 × 3 = 5 + 21 = 26. (17 is the value for term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 10?
items.e: From term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps of 6: 100 − 9 × 6 = 100 − 54 = 46. (76 is the value for term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: Make a table of values: figure number and number of craft sticks. How many craft sticks will Figure 6 need?
items.e: The table starts 4, 7, 10 and goes up by 3. From Figure 1 to Figure 6 there are 5 jumps: 4 + 5 × 3 = 19.

items.q: Make a table of values: figure number and number of tiles. How many tiles will Figure 8 need?
items.e: The table starts 3, 5, 7 and goes up by 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 8 there are 7 jumps: 3 + 7 × 2 = 17.

items.q: Make a table of values: figure number and number of tiles. How many tiles will Figure 6 need?
items.e: The table starts 5, 9, 13 and goes up by 4. From Figure 1 to Figure 6 there are 5 jumps: 5 + 5 × 4 = 25.

items.q: Make a table of values: figure number and number of tiles. How many tiles will Figure 7 need?
items.e: The table starts 4, 6, 8 and goes up by 2. From Figure 1 to Figure 7 there are 6 jumps: 4 + 6 × 2 = 16.

items.q: The pattern continues. Which term number has a term value of 40?
items.e: Count the jumps: 40 − 4 = 36, and 36 ÷ 3 = 12 jumps after term 1. So it is term 13. (40 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern continues. Which term number has a term value of 14?
items.e: Count the jumps down: 50 − 14 = 36, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9 jumps after term 1. So it is term 10. (14 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q: The pattern continues. Which term number has a term value of 75?
items.e: Count the jumps: 75 − 5 = 70, and 70 ÷ 5 = 14 jumps after term 1. So it is term 15. (75 is the term value, not the term number.)

items.q:
Which list follows the pattern rule?
Start at 7 and add 4 each time.
items.e: Start at 7 and add 4: 7, 11, 15, 19. (Swapping gives 4, 11, 18, 25, which starts at 4 and adds 7.)

items.q:
Which list follows the pattern rule?
Start at 50 and subtract 6 each time.
items.e: Start at 50 and subtract 6: 50, 44, 38, 32. The first term is the start number, 50.

items.q:
Which list follows the pattern rule?
Start at 20 and add 5 each time.
items.e: Start at 20 and add 5: 20, 25, 30, 35. (Swapping gives 5, 25, 45, 65, which starts at 5 and adds 20.)

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
96, 48, 24, 12, …
c: Start at 48 and divide by 2 each time.
Start at 96 and subtract 24 each time.
Start at 96 and divide by 2 each time.
Start at 96 and subtract 48 each time.
items.e: Each term is half of the one before: 96 ÷ 2 = 48, 48 ÷ 2 = 24, 24 ÷ 2 = 12. “Subtract 48” works only for the first step.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
2, 4, 8, 16, …
c: Start at 4 and multiply by 2 each time.
Start at 2 and add 4 each time.
Start at 2 and add 2 each time.
Start at 2 and multiply by 2 each time.
items.e: Each term is 2 times the one before: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. “Add 2” works only for the first step.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
3, 9, 15, 21, …
c: Start at 3 and multiply by 3 each time.
Start at 6 and add 3 each time.
Start at 9 and add 6 each time.
Start at 3 and add 6 each time.
items.e: Each term is 6 more than the one before. “Multiply by 3” works for 3 → 9 but not for 9 → 15.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
4, 8, 12, 16, …
c: Start at 4 and multiply by 2 each time.
Start at 4 and add 8 each time.
Start at 8 and add 4 each time.
Start at 4 and add 4 each time.
items.e: Each term is 4 more than the one before. “Multiply by 2” works for 4 → 8 but not for 8 → 12.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
100, 93, 86, 79, …
c: Start at 100 and subtract 7 each time.
Start at 100 and add 7 each time.
Start at 93 and subtract 7 each time.
Start at 79 and subtract 7 each time.
items.e: The first term is 100, and each term is 7 less than the one before: 100 − 7 = 93, 93 − 7 = 86.

items.q: Which rule gives the term value from the term number?
items.e: The term value goes up by 5, so multiply the term number by 5. Term 1: 1 × 5 = 5, and the value is 3, so subtract 2. Check term 4: 4 × 5 − 2 = 18. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value from the term number?
items.e: The term value goes up by 10, so multiply the term number by 10. Term 1: 1 × 10 = 10, and the value is 15, so add 5. Check term 4: 4 × 10 + 5 = 45. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value from the term number?
items.e: The term value goes up by 3, so multiply the term number by 3. Term 1: 1 × 3 = 3, and the value is 4, so add 1. Check term 4: 4 × 3 + 1 = 13. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value from the term number?
items.e: The term value goes up by 4, so multiply the term number by 4. Term 1: 1 × 4 = 4, and the value is 7, so add 3. Check term 4: 4 × 4 + 3 = 19. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: Which rule gives the term value from the term number?
items.e: The term value goes up by 2, so multiply the term number by 2. Term 1: 1 × 2 = 2, and the value is 7, so add 5. Check term 4: 4 × 2 + 5 = 13. (A rule must work for every term, not only term 1.)

items.q: The pattern 2, 7, 12, 17, … continues. Which number will be in the pattern?
items.e: Every term is 2 plus a number of jumps of 5. 52 − 2 = 50, and 50 ÷ 5 = 10 jumps, so 52 is term 11. For the other numbers, the difference from 2 is not a multiple of 5.

items.q: The pattern 5, 9, 13, 17, … continues. Which number will be in the pattern?
items.e: Every term is 5 plus a number of jumps of 4. 41 − 5 = 36, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9 jumps, so 41 is term 10. For the other numbers, the difference from 5 is not a multiple of 4.

items.q: The pattern 4, 7, 10, 13, … continues. Which number will be in the pattern?
items.e: Every term is 4 plus a number of jumps of 3. 46 − 4 = 42, and 42 ÷ 3 = 14 jumps, so 46 is term 15. For the other numbers, the difference from 4 is not a multiple of 3.

items.q: The pattern 6, 12, 18, 24, … continues. Which number will be in the pattern?
items.e: Every term is 6 plus a number of jumps of 6. 84 − 6 = 78, and 78 ÷ 6 = 13 jumps, so 84 is term 14. For the other numbers, the difference from 6 is not a multiple of 6.

items.q: A bracelet repeats red, white, white, red, white, white, … In which position is the 10th red bead?
items.e: The red beads are in positions 1, 4, 7, … (start at 1 and add 3). The 10th red bead is 9 jumps after the first: 1 + 9 × 3 = 28. (10 × 3 = 30 counts one jump too many.)

items.q: Emma strings beads in a repeating pattern: red, blue, green, yellow, red, blue, green, yellow, … What colour is the 30th bead?
items.e: The core has 4 beads. 30 ÷ 4 = 7 R 2, so after 7 full cores the 30th bead is the 2nd bead of the core: blue.

items.q: Owen draws shapes in a repeating pattern: circle, square, triangle, star, circle, square, … What is the 43rd shape?
items.e: The core has 4 shapes. 43 ÷ 4 = 10 R 3, so the 43rd shape is the 3rd shape of the core: triangle.

items.q: Here is a pattern rule: Start at 12 and add 5 each time. What is the term value for term number 10?
items.e: From term 1 to term 10 there are 9 jumps of 5: 12 + 9 × 5 = 12 + 45 = 57. (Term 1 is the start number, so there are only 9 jumps.)

items.q: Here is a pattern rule: Start at 8 and add 7 each time. What is the term value for term number 20?
items.e: From term 1 to term 20 there are 19 jumps of 7: 8 + 19 × 7 = 8 + 133 = 141. (Term 1 is the start number, so there are only 19 jumps.)

items.q: Here is a pattern rule: Start at 200 and subtract 15 each time. What is the term value for term number 12?
items.e: From term 1 to term 12 there are 11 jumps of 15: 200 − 11 × 15 = 200 − 165 = 35. (Term 1 is the start number, so there are only 11 jumps.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
6.3, 5.9, 5.5, ?
items.e: The pattern subtracts 0.4 each time. 5.5 − 0.4 = 5.1. (5.9 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
2.45, 2.55, 2.65, ?
items.e: The pattern adds 0.1 (one tenth) each time: the tenths digit goes up by 1. 2.65 + 0.1 = 2.75. (2.66 adds one hundredth.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.25, 0.5, 0.75, ?
items.e: The pattern adds 0.25 each time. 0.75 + 0.25 = 1. (75 hundredths + 25 hundredths = 100 hundredths = 1 whole, not 0.100.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.3, 0.6, 0.9, ?
items.e: The pattern adds 0.3 each time. 0.9 + 0.3 = 1.2, because 9 tenths + 3 tenths = 12 tenths = 1 and 2 tenths. (0.12 is twelve hundredths.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, ?
items.e: The pattern adds 0.5 (five tenths) each time. 3 + 0.5 = 3.5. (3.05 adds 5 hundredths, not 5 tenths.)

items.q: The pattern 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, … continues. What is the 10th term?
items.e: Each term is the term number × 0.5 (half of the term number). Term 10: 10 × 0.5 = 5. (4.5 is term 9.)
2.25 + 0.75 = 3, because 25 hundredths + 75 hundredths = 100 hundredths = 1 whole. (2.1 comes from writing 2.100: the 100 hundredths are 1 whole, so they go to the ones.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
3, 2.75, 2.5, 2.25, ?
items.e: The pattern subtracts 0.25 each time. 2.25 − 0.25 = 2. (1.75 subtracts twice; 2.05 subtracts 0.2.)

items.q: The pattern 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, … continues. What is the 8th term?
items.e: Each term is the term number × 0.25 (a quarter). Term 8: 8 × 0.25 = 2. (1.25 is term 5, the next term in the list.)

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The value goes up by 2.5 each time. 7.5 + 2.5 = 10, because 0.5 + 0.5 = 1 whole. (9.10 forgets to regroup the 10 tenths.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 8?
items.e: The value goes down by 0.5 each time. From term 1 to term 8 there are 7 jumps: 7 × 0.5 = 3.5, and 10 − 3.5 = 6.5. (6 uses 8 jumps.)

items.q: What is the missing term value?
items.e: The value goes up by 0.4 each time. 0.8 + 0.4 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 + 0.4 = 1.6. (0.12 is twelve hundredths.)

items.q: The pattern continues in the same way. What is the term value for term number 10?
items.e: Each term is the term number × 0.05 (5 hundredths). Term 10: 10 × 0.05 = 0.5. (0.25 is term 5.)

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, …
c: Start at 0.25 and add 0.5 each time.
Start at 0.5 and multiply by 2 each time.
Start at 0.25 and multiply by 2 each time.
Start at 0.25 and add 0.25 each time.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
0.5, 1.25, 2, 2.75, …
c: Start at 0.75 and add 0.5 each time.
Start at 0.5 and add 0.75 each time.
Start at 1.25 and add 0.75 each time.
Start at 0.5 and add 0.25 each time.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
3.2, 3.4, 3.6, 3.8, …
c: Start at 3.2 and add 0.02 each time.
Start at 3.4 and add 0.2 each time.
Start at 3.2 and add 2 each time.
Start at 3.2 and add 0.2 each time.
items.e: The tenths digit goes up by 2 each time, so the pattern adds 0.2 (2 tenths): 3.2 + 0.2 = 3.4.

items.q:
Which pattern rule describes this pattern?
5, 4.75, 4.5, 4.25, …
c: Start at 5 and subtract 0.25 each time.
Start at 5 and add 0.25 each time.
Start at 5 and subtract 0.75 each time.
Start at 4.75 and subtract 0.25 each time.
items.e: 5 − 0.25 = 4.75, 4.75 − 0.25 = 4.5, 4.5 − 0.25 = 4.25. The terms get smaller, so the rule subtracts.

items.q:
What is the next term?
4.97, 4.98, 4.99, ?
items.e: The pattern adds 0.01 each time. 4.99 + 0.01 = 5, because 99 hundredths + 1 hundredth = 1 whole. (4.1 comes from writing 4.100: the 100 hundredths are 1 whole, so they go to the ones.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
0.03, 0.3, 3, 30, ?
items.e: Each term is 10 times the one before: the digits move one place to the left. 30 × 10 = 300. (33 adds 3.)

items.q:
What is the next term?
7000, 700, 70, 7, ?
items.e: Each term is the one before ÷ 10: the digits move one place to the right. 7 ÷ 10 = 0.7. (0.07 divides by 100.)

items.q: A sap tank on a maple farm has 40 L of sap at 8 a.m. Sap drips in at 2.5 L each hour. How much sap is in the tank at 2 p.m.?
items.e: 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. is 6 hours. 6 × 2.5 = 15 L. 40 + 15 = 55 L. (15 L forgets the 40 L already in the tank.)

items.q: On a winter afternoon it is 9 °C at 3 p.m. The temperature falls 1.5 °C each hour. What is the temperature at 7 p.m.?
items.e: 3 p.m. to 7 p.m. is 4 hours. 4 × 1.5 = 6 degrees. 9 − 6 = 3 °C. (15 °C adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: During a snowstorm, there is 10 cm of snow on the ground at noon. Snow piles up 2.5 cm each hour. How deep is the snow at 4 p.m.?
items.e: Noon to 4 p.m. is 4 hours. 4 × 2.5 = 10 cm. 10 + 10 = 20 cm. ((10 + 2.5) × 4 = 50 adds the starting snow every hour.)

items.q: The graph shows the pages Ava has left to read in her book at the end of each day. Which pattern rule matches the graph?
c: Start at 25 and subtract 10 each day.
Start at 25 and add 5 each day.
Start at 30 and subtract 5 each day.
Start at 25 and subtract 5 each day.
items.e: The first point is 25, and each point is 5 lower: 25, 20, 15, 10. So start at 25 and subtract 5 each day.

items.q: Benjamin builds a row of triangles with toothpicks. 1 triangle uses 3, 2 triangles use 5 and 3 triangles use 7. How many toothpicks does he need for 15 triangles?
items.e: Each new triangle adds 2 toothpicks. From 1 to 15 triangles there are 14 jumps: 3 + 14 × 2 = 31. (15 × 3 = 45 counts the shared sides twice.)

items.q: Square tables are pushed together in a row for a class party. 1 table seats 4 students, 2 tables seat 6, and 3 tables seat 8. How many students can sit at 10 tables?
items.e: Each new table adds 2 seats. From 1 table to 10 tables there are 9 jumps: 4 + 9 × 2 = 22. (10 × 4 = 40 counts seats lost where the tables touch.)

items.q: A candle is 20 cm tall. It burns down 1.5 cm each hour. How tall is it after 6 hours?
items.e: 6 × 1.5 = 9 cm burns away. 20 − 9 = 11 cm. (9 cm is the part that burned.)

items.q: In March the snow in Nathan’s backyard melts by the same amount each day. On which day will the snow be 12 cm deep?
items.e: The snow goes down 3 cm a day: 30, 27, 24, 21, 18, 15, 12. That is day 7. (12 is the depth, not the day.)

items.q: Lucas makes a row of squares with craft sticks: 4 sticks, 7 sticks, 10 sticks, … Which figure uses 31 sticks?
items.e: The sticks go up by 3. 31 − 4 = 27, and 27 ÷ 3 = 9 jumps after Figure 1, so it is Figure 10. (31 is the number of sticks, not the figure number.)

items.q: Swimming lessons cost $15 to sign up plus $8 for each lesson. Hana pays $79 in total. How many lessons does she take?
items.e: Take away the $15 first: 79 − 15 = 64. Then 64 ÷ 8 = 8 lessons. Check: 15 + 8 × 8 = $79. (64 is the cost of the lessons.)

items.q: Each point is (day, height). Which point will come next on the graph?
items.e: The next day is day 5. The height goes up 3 cm: 11 + 3 = 14. The point is (5, 14). (In (14, 5) the numbers are swapped: the day comes first.)

items.q: To train for the Terry Fox Run, Maya runs 1.5 km in week 1. Each week she runs 0.5 km more. How far does she run in week 6?
items.e: From week 1 to week 6 there are 5 jumps: 5 × 0.5 = 2.5 km. 1.5 + 2.5 = 4 km. (4.5 km uses 6 jumps.)

items.q: The graph shows how much money Liam has saved after each week. The pattern continues. How much will he have after week 7?
items.e: The points go up $4 each week: 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32. After week 7 he has $32. (7 × 8 = 56 multiplies the first value.)

items.q: One paper cup is 12 cm tall. Each extra cup on the stack adds 1.5 cm. How tall is a stack of 10 cups?
items.e: The first cup is 12 cm. There are 9 extra cups: 9 × 1.5 = 13.5 cm. 12 + 13.5 = 25.5 cm. (27 cm counts 10 extra cups.)

items.q: Today is Monday. Days of the week repeat every 7 days. What day of the week will it be 30 days from today?
items.e: 30 ÷ 7 = 4 R 2. After 4 full weeks (28 days) it is Monday again. 2 more days: Wednesday.

items.q: Ava puts a quarter (25¢) in a jar every day. How much money is in the jar after 12 days?
items.e: Count by 0.25: 4 quarters make $1, so 12 quarters make $3.00. 12 × 0.25 = 3. ($300 forgets that 25¢ is $0.25.)

items.q: Zoe’s bean plant grows the same amount each day. How tall will it be on day 8?
items.e: It grows 3 cm a day. From day 1 to day 8 there are 7 jumps: 2 + 7 × 3 = 23 cm. (14 cm is day 5, the next point.)

items.q: Priya has $20 in her piggy bank. She saves $5 each week. How much will she have after 9 weeks?
items.e: She adds 9 × $5 = $45 to her $20: 20 + 45 = $65. ($45 forgets the $20 she started with.)

items.q: Mei has 120 hockey cards. She gives away 6 cards each week. After how many weeks will she have 48 cards left?
items.e: She gives away 120 − 48 = 72 cards. 72 ÷ 6 = 12 weeks. (48 ÷ 6 = 8 uses the cards left, not the cards given away.)

items.q: Liam keeps saving in the same way. In which week will he have $48 saved?
items.e: From $20 in week 4, he needs 48 − 20 = $28 more. 28 ÷ 4 = 7 more weeks: 4 + 7 = week 11. (48 is the number of dollars, not the week.)
